title: Hiring Radar: Portfolio Fit Scan Template
content:
Purpose: Provide a lightweight, repeatable template (the ‘hiring radar’) to evaluate candidate portfolio fit as an early gate in role-level hiring flows. Use this scan to decide whether to proceed to structured interviews or to suggest alternative role matches/internal referrals. The goal is to reduce interview cost, surface signal early, and improve candidate experience with clear feedback and next steps.

Scope: Intended for IC and early-senior hires across product, infra, and platform teams. Best used for candidate portfolios (repos, deployed demos, design docs, research notes, small projects). Not a replacement for full technical interviews — it’s a pre-screen and calibration artifact for hiring managers and recruiters.

When to run:
- Right after initial resume/LinkedIn screen and prior to booking technical panel.
- For internal referrals where portfolio may be small but contextual fit is high.
- When role requires cross-team experience (platform + product) and we need early evidence of cross-functional work.

How to use (quick):
1) Recruiter or hiring manager runs the scan (10–25 minutes).
2) Populate the short checklist and a single-paragraph verdict.
3) If portfolio meets criteria => trigger structured interview scheduling. If marginal => route to hiring manager for quick call. If negative => send concise feedback + suggested next steps (e.g., build X, try take-home).

Role archetypes covered:
- Production-platform engineer (ops + infra changes visible in repos/infra-as-code)
- Model serving/ML infra (model checkpoints + eval harnesses + perf traces)
- Product engineer (end-to-end feature: issue -> PR -> metrics/dashboard)
- Data/Applied ML (reproducible experiments, evaluation notebooks, small pipeline)

Portfolio-fit checklist (Y/N/Notes) — quick items to capture:
- Relevance: Portfolio shows work in topology similar to the role (e.g., model-serving repo for serving role).
- Ownership: Candidate owned a clear vertical (issue threads, PRs, or a summary that indicates ownership).
- Depth: One example with moderate depth (non-trivial design, tradeoffs, performance or scalability considerations).
- Reproducibility: Repo has README, runnable instructions, tests or a reproducible demo.
- Communication: Clear README and PR descriptions; design doc available if relevant.
- Impact: Evidence of measurable outcomes (metrics, reduced latency, reduced cost, adoption).
- Engineering hygiene: Tests, CI config, linting, sensible commit history.
- Signal for collaboration: Linked issues, reviewer comments, cross-team PRs.
- Security/privacy considerations present if applicable (e.g., redaction, KMS usage notes).
- Accessibility of artifacts (not behind private paywalls; runnable with limited setup).

Scoring (quick): For each item mark: Yes = 2, Partial = 1, No = 0. Sum and interpret: >=15 strong fit, 10–14 proceed with standard panel, 6–9 conditional (manager call/take-home), <=5 likely mismatch. Always add a short rationale sentence.

Interview rubric suggestions (for next-stage structured panel) — include this in the verdict when recommending next steps:
- System design / architecture: 1–5 scale; focus on tradeoffs, scaling, operational costs, observability. Example probe: design a low-latency batched inference gateway for multi-tenant workloads.
- Code crafting: 1–5 scale; small pairing task or take-home focusing on reliability and testability. Example probe: implement a KV cache with TTL and eviction for model contexts.
- Domain knowledge: 1–5 scale; model life-cycle, quantization basics, inference optimization signals depending on role.
- Collaboration & communication: 1–5 scale; ability to write a clear README/design doc and negotiate scope.
- Ownership & impact: 1–5 scale; evidence that candidate shipped features end-to-end and measured outcomes.
- Bias & safety checks: 1–5 scale; probe for thoughtful handling of data, privacy, and potential misuse.

Example structured micro-interview plan (40–60 minutes):
- 5 min: context & clarifying Qs (interviewer: hiring manager).
- 15 min: system design (interviewer: senior eng).
- 15 min: coding/pairing (interviewer: peer).
- 10 min: behavioral/impact (interviewer: PM or cross-functional partner).
- 5 min: candidate questions & next steps.

Scoring template for panelists (flat text to paste into debrief):
- Candidate: [name] | Role: [role] | Stage: portfolio-scan => panel
- Portfolio-scan score: [0–20] — short rationale (1–2 sentences)
- Panel averages: architecture [x], code [x], domain [x], collab [x], ownership [x]; recommendation: hire / no-hire / hire-with-conditions / more-time

Onboarding quick-start: 14-day condensed checklist (deliverable-oriented, aimed at reducing ramp time for hires selected via this flow)
Day 0–1:
- Accesses: GitHub org, internal Confluence, team Slack, infra read-only dashboards. Checklist: confirm SSO, 2FA, minimal local dev VM.
- Buddy assigned: shadow buddy (same subdomain) + schedule 30-min sync in first 48 hours.

Day 2–4:
- Small first task: triage a low-risk issue from the team backlog; submit a draft PR with test; buddy reviews. Objective: flow of code -> review -> CI.
- Documentation task: improve README of onboarding repo with a missing step and submit PR (helps confirm permissions).

Day 5–10:
- Feature iteration: ship a non-customer-facing improvement (observability, minor perf tweak, or test coverage) with owner-style notes.
- Cross-team sync: 30-min intro call with dependent service owners.

Day 11–14:
- Post-mortem lite: document a small decision made, its tradeoffs, and a retrospective note.
- Success check: hiring manager marks early signals (list below) and sets 30/60/90 objectives.

Early signals of successful ramp (to be captured at day 14):
- Completed PRs with quality review comments addressed.
- Able to explain the team’s critical path in a 5-minute walkthrough.
- Demonstrated basic knowledge of deployment and rollbacks.
- Proactively raised one improvement idea with an actionable plan.

Templates & communication snippets (short):
- Candidate feedback (if portfolio not a fit): "Thanks for sharing your work — we found strong elements in [X], but the specific experience we need for this role is [Y]. We encourage you to try [Z] and reapply; if you’d like feedback, we can share 2–3 actionable suggestions."
- Manager instruction to recruiter: "Run the Hiring Radar on all inbound portfolios for this role. If score >=15, auto-schedule panel; if 10–14, triage call; <10 — close with written feedback."

Calibration notes (to add to weekly hiring sync):
- Run 10 random portfolio scans across open roles and review divergence across two hiring managers — capture where scoring diverges >4 points and iterate the rubric.
- Keep an annotated exemplar portfolio per archetype in Confluence with comments and redactions for reference.

Open issues / TODOs:
- Add a small checklist to the ATS for auto-tagging portfolio artifacts.
- Create a short video walkthrough (3–5 min) showing an ideal candidate writeup for hiring managers.
- Add a privacy checklist item for candidate-hosted datasets (masking, sample sizes).

Notes on fairness & bias:
- The scan is intentionally narrow: do not use it to filter on prestigious signals (university/company names) alone. Focus on evidence of work, reproducibility, and clear communication.
- If portfolio shows heavy reliance on team-owned repos (no author-specific commits), ask for a short note from the candidate describing their contribution.

Appendix: example portfolio questions to ask candidates in a follow-up call:
- Tell us about the part of this project you owned end-to-end. What were two tradeoffs you considered?
- Describe a production incident you resolved — what monitoring alerted you, how you triaged, and what follow-up you implemented?
- How do you measure success for a change that reduces inference latency but might increase cost?

References & exemplars: add links to 2–3 anonymized exemplar portfolios in Confluence (referenced in linked_artifacts).

Owner notes: maintain this template in the shared hiring kit, and update after each hiring cohort with recorded calibration notes (tag: hiring-radar).

Contact: Maya Thompson (people-ops) — DM in Slack or add to hiring-radar@redwood.internal for scheduling a calibration run.
